title: A Friend Loves at All Times

verses.text: Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.
A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son and share his inheritance as one of the brothers.
A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD is the tester of hearts.
A wicked man listens to evil lips; a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.
He who mocks the poor insults their Maker; whoever gloats over calamity will not go unpunished.
Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of a son is his father.
Eloquent words are unfit for a fool; how much worse are lying lips to a ruler!
A bribe is a charm to its giver; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.
An evil man seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
A man lacking judgment strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.
He who loves transgression loves strife; he who builds his gate high invites destruction.
The one with a perverse heart finds no good, and he whose tongue is deceitful falls into trouble.
A man fathers a fool to his own grief; the father of a fool has no joy.
A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.
A wicked man takes a covert bribe to subvert the course of justice.
Wisdom is the focus of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to her who bore him.
It is surely not good to punish the innocent or to flog a noble for his honesty.
A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit.
Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent, and discerning when he holds his tongue.

context.author: Solomon, named in the heading “The proverbs of Solomon” (10:1). The collection runs from 10:1 to 22:16, about 375 sayings.
context.genre: Wisdom sayings: two-line proverbs, most of them contrasts
context.audience: Anyone learning to live wisely, first the young men of Israel’s court and households
context.mapLabel: JERUSALEM, THE ROYAL COURT OF SOLOMON
context.setting: “Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife” (v.1). The LORD tests hearts as the furnace tests silver and gold (v.3). Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends (v.9). Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam (v.14). “A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity” (v.17). A joyful heart is good medicine (v.22), and even a fool is thought wise if he keeps silent (v.28).
context.custom: Silver and gold were refined in clay crucibles over hot fires to burn off the dross (v.3; Malachi 3:3). Dams and channels held water for fields and towns, and a small leak soon became a flood (v.14). A bribe hidden in the fold of a cloak (v.23) was the way a judge was bought, though the law forbade it (Exodus 23:8).
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 18 warns against the loner and against the harm of hasty words.
context.timelineBible: David and Jonathan are the Bible’s great picture of loyal friendship (1 Samuel 18:1-4; 20:17). The refining of silver as a picture of God testing hearts comes again in Psalm 66:10 and Malachi 3:3.

translation.meaning: A neighbor, companion or friend. The friend of v.17 stays loyal in good times and bad.
A melting pot for refining silver.
A gift given to twist justice.

gospelParallels.note: No greater love than to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.
Faith refined by fire, more precious than gold.

otBackground.note: He will sit as a refiner of silver.

overview.summary: Quiet is better than feasting with strife; the LORD tests hearts, a true friend loves at all times, and a cheerful heart is good medicine.
overview.settingLine: Sayings about peace, friendship and quiet words.

history.t: Silver was purified in a crucible.

customs.t: Loyalty was tested in hard times.

archaeology.t: Hoards of cut silver pieces (hacksilber) show silver used as money by weight.
Shafts and tunnels at Megiddo and Hazor brought water inside the walls.

overview.discussion: “A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity” (v.17). Who has been that friend to me, and whose friend can I be in a hard time now?
overview.book: The book of Proverbs · 31 chapters. Short sayings and longer poems that teach how to live wisely in God’s world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.
overview.author: Solomon (10:1)
